newsitem.title: POLAND: Final ordeal faces Poland before floods end.
newsitem.headline: Final ordeal faces Poland before floods end.

text.p: Poles fought the last round of their three-week flood disaster on Friday as surges of high water on the Odra (Oder) river strained against leaky dikes.
"Our worst problem is maintaining the anti-flood dikes. They are as soaked as a sponge," national crisis committee spokesman Krzysztof Pomes told Reuters in Warsaw.

One high-water swell, having largely spared the city of Opole from a repeat of its earlier heavy flooding, was due to reach the major centre of Wroclaw later in the day as it headed north to the German border and the sea.
Wroclaw spokesman Aleksander Wozny said the swell, caused by rains last weekend over heavily-flooded west and south Poland, was lower than at first feared.

He said no repeat of the floods that turned Wroclaw city centre streets into raging torrents two weeks ago was now expected but the coming 12-hour onslaught threatened outlying settlements that were home to tens of thousands of people.
In Wroclaw and along the entire river teams of troops and volunteers shored up sandbag walls and waited to pounce on any signs of weakness in defences to avoid a break.

The swell approaching Wroclaw in the southwest is a lesser repeat of an initial northward rush of water early in July when floods inundated 6,000 sq kms of Poland, struck more than 1,200 towns and villages and killed 55 people.
That crest of water, now much diminished, was now approaching the port city of Szczecin on the sea.
But continued high water was wreaking havoc elsewhere on the river especially where it runs along the German border.
A second dike burst overnight south of the German city Frankfurt an der Oder, prompting the evacuation of thousands from nearby villages.
So massive was the flow into the German countryside that it eased the pressure further north on the river, officials said.
Poland's Meteorology and Water Economy Institute said scattered rain and thunderstorms were expected over Poland at the weekend and Monday, but after that sun would appear.

It said the rains were not expected to be heavy enough to cause a new round of the disaster, although falls over the southern mountains, feeding later into the Wisla (Vistula) river might raise water levels.
Hundreds of towns and villages were still partly flooded, and dozens were completely under water. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
